title: Explainable token-level SLI attribution and multi-region failover orchestration
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build an explainable instrumentation and dashboarding flow that ties token-level latency SLIs to upstream causes (KV cache hit rate, batching distribution, model variant, region, and admission decisions) and surfaces actionable signals for multi-region failover and circuit breakers. Deliverables: Prometheus/Tracing queries, dashboard panels, a lightweight causal scoring algorithm for each anomaly, synthetic prefix probers to stress mixed-length workloads, and operational runbooks describing graceful rollback and circuit tuning. Goal is fast triage (under 10 minutes) from SLI alert to likely remediation action and automated suggestions for failover policies.
background: Current token-SLI dashboards show p50/p95/p99 but lack correlated causal context (e.g., sudden kv-hit drop, batch size spikes).
Operators spend too long mapping tail latency spikes to configuration drivers when failovers are triggered in the wild.
We need explainability to reduce MTTR and make automatic failover decisions more defensible for on-call and platform teams.
goals: Create token-level SLI panels that annotate probable root causes with confidence scores.
Instrument prefix-skewed synthetic probes that mimic real customer mixed-length workloads and feed into golden-signal baselines.
Expose migration-friendly runbook actions and one-click rollback suggestions in the console dashboard.
Feed attribution signals into the failover orchestrator to enable graded, explainable regional failover decisions.
non_goals: Full causal inference research; lightweight, explainable heuristics only (no heavy Bayesian model).
Re-implement end-to-end traffic routing—this ticket only produces signals and recommended policy changes.
tasks: Design metric set and labels: token_duration_ms (by shard, region, model_variant, batch_size, kv_hit), kv_hit_rate, batch_size_histogram, admission_decision, tenant_id (anonymized)
Implement Prometheus exporters and tracing spans to emit token_duration_ms with context tags (PR: github.com/redwood/infra-exporter/pull/ TBD).
Create synthetic prefix prober that generates weighted prefix lengths and measures kv_hit vs token latency correlation.
Prototype an attribution scoring heuristic: change-point detection + weighted contribution from correlated metrics over a 2-10s window.
Dashboard buildout: overview panel, per-tenant cohort panels, causal annotation timeline, and suggested-failover button wired to a feature-flagged API.
Integrate confidence scores into failover orchestrator simulation environment for operator review.
acceptance_criteria: Prometheus queries available for token_duration_ms breakdowns by region/model_variant/batch_size/kv_hit.
Attribution heuristic implemented as a library function and exercised by unit tests with synthetic anomalies.
Dashboard screens implemented in Console with causal annotations visible for at least three distinct simulated failure modes (kv drop, batching surge, model fallback).
Synthetic prober runs continuously in staging and produces a baseline dataset used by the dashboard.
Runbook section exists describing operator steps mapped to dashboard annotation types and an automated suggestion for failover policy (dry-run).
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Spike completed for exporter schema; added token_duration_ms tagset (region, model_variant, batch_size, kv_hit).
2025-02-14: First-pass synthetic prober ready in staging; observed expected correlation between kv_hit_rate drop and p99 growth for long prefixes.
2025-02-16: Prototype attribution heuristic (change-point + weighted correlation) yields reasonable labels on simulated incidents; confidence score normalized 0-1.
2025-02-18: Dashboard wireframes uploaded to Confluence and initial panels implemented in console feature branch (console-2025.02-feature/sli-attrib).
review_feedback: PM review (Lena Cho): Request to ensure per-tenant privacy: only cohort-level identifiers in public dashboards.
Design review (Marco Li): Suggests compact timeline annotations and colorblind-safe palette for confidence bands.
SRE review (Ibrahim Khan): Wants throttling on synthetic prober to avoid polluting production admission quotas; recommend staging-only by default.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: Use lightweight heuristic (change-point detection + Pearson partial correlation) instead of heavy causal models to keep latency small and make explanations human-readable.
Tradeoff: Attribution will be probabilistic and occasionally ambiguous for multi-causal incidents; surfaced confidence scores and links to raw traces for deep-dive.
Decision: Synthetic prober runs in staging by default; may run limited low-rate probes in production under a feature flag with strict quota.
runbook_snippets: When dashboard shows 'kv_hit_drop' with confidence > 0.7: check shard-level cache metrics and if sustained > 60s, trigger cache rewarm workflow.
When 'batch_spike' detected and admission rate increase > 2x: consider reducing burst policy on region or enable temporary admission cap for P1 tenants.
If 'model_variant_fallback' annotated: validate model variant health and if degraded, activate preset fallback routing to dedicated-region variant.
queries_examples: PromQL: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_duration_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, region, model_variant, kv_hit))
PromQL: increase(kv_hits_total[1m]) / increase(kv_lookups_total[1m]) as kv_hit_rate (implemented as separate metric labels)
Trace query: find traces with token_duration_ms > 200ms and group by batch_size and kv_hit tag to generate causal candidates.
notes: Keep all telemetry tags lightweight to avoid high cardinality explosion. Consider cardinality bucketization for tenant_id (cohorts: small/medium/large) and prefix_length (short/medium/long).
Plan to evaluate false-positive rate of attribution heuristic during chaos week (2025-02-25) using injected kv miss and batch spikes.
